content: Azelaic acid is an FDA-approved topical medication primarily used for the treatment of mild to moderate rosacea, specifically targeting inflammatory papules and pustules. It is also recognized for its antibacterial and anti-acne properties. However, its efficacy in treating erythema associated with rosacea in the absence of papules and pustules has not been established. Administration and Dosage: For adults: A thin layer of Finacea Gel (15%) should be gently applied to the affected areas of the face twice daily, in the morning and evening. Patients should be reassessed if no improvement is observed after 12 weeks of therapy. Off-label use: Azelaic acid 20% cream can be applied topically twice daily. However, there is limited information regarding off-label guideline-supported use in adults. Pediatric use: There is limited data on the safety and efficacy of azelaic acid in pediatric patients, both for FDA-labeled and off-label uses. Contraindications: Finacea Gel (15%) is contraindicated in individuals with a known hypersensitivity to propylene glycol or any other component of the formulation. Warnings and Precautions: Finacea Gel (15%) is for dermatologic use only and should not be used in the eyes, orally, or intravaginally. Rare cases of hypopigmentation have been reported, particularly in patients with darker skin tones. These patients should be monitored for early signs of hypopigmentation. Contact with the eyes should be avoided. If accidental contact occurs, the eyes should be rinsed thoroughly with water, and a physician should be consulted if irritation persists. If severe irritation or sensitivity develops, treatment should be discontinued, and appropriate therapy should be initiated. In animal studies, chronic use of Finacea Gel was associated with an increased incidence of papillomas at the treatment site. The clinical relevance of these findings to humans is unclear. Adverse Reactions: Common side effects include pruritus, stinging, burning, and tingling sensations at the application site. Rarely reported adverse effects include worsening of asthma, vitiligo-like depigmentation, hypertrichosis, and exacerbation of recurrent herpes labialis. Use in Specific Populations: Pregnancy: Azelaic acid is classified as Pregnancy Category B by the FDA. There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Animal studies have shown embryotoxicity at high oral doses associated with maternal toxicity. Azelaic acid should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. Nursing mothers: Less than 4% of a topically applied dose is systemically absorbed, and the uptake into maternal milk is not expected to cause significant changes. However, caution is advised when administering Finacea Gel to nursing mothers. Geriatric use: Clinical studies did not include sufficient numbers of subjects aged 65 and older to determine whether they respond differently from younger subjects. Renal and hepatic impairment: There is no specific FDA guidance on the use of azelaic acid in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. Pharmacology: The exact mechanism of action of azelaic acid in rosacea is unknown. It is a naturally occurring saturated dicarboxylic acid. Azelaic acid is minimally metabolized in the skin and is primarily excreted unchanged in the urine. Some β-oxidation to shorter-chain dicarboxylic acids occurs. Clinical Studies: Finacea Gel (15%) was evaluated in two multicenter, randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled 12-week studies involving 664 patients with mild to moderate papulopustular rosacea. The gel demonstrated statistically significant efficacy in reducing inflammatory lesions compared to the vehicle. However, its efficacy in treating erythema without papules and pustules has not been evaluated. Patient Counseling Information: Patients should use Finacea Gel (15%) only as directed by their physician and for external use only. The affected areas should be cleansed with a mild soap or soapless cleansing lotion and patted dry before application. Patients should avoid spicy foods, thermally hot foods and drinks, and alcoholic beverages, as these may exacerbate rosacea symptoms. Hands should be washed after applying the gel. Cosmetics may be applied after the gel has dried. Patients should report any abnormal changes in skin color to their physician. Storage: Finacea Gel (15%) should be stored at 25°C (77°F), with excursions permitted between 15–30°C (59–86°F). Overdose: Acute overdose is unlikely as Finacea Gel is intended for cutaneous use only. If pronounced local irritation occurs, treatment should be discontinued, and appropriate therapy should be initiated. Brand Name: Finacea® is the brand name for azelaic acid gel (15%). This detailed information provides a comprehensive understanding of azelaic acid, its uses, administration, precautions, and potential side effects, ensuring safe and effective use under medical supervision.
